changes_vs_current: New topic. Gut check (12 answers, written before any source was read): All I Want for Christmas Is You, Jingle Bells, Silent Night, White Christmas, Rudolph, Frosty, Jingle Bell Rock, Rockin' Around, Santa Claus Is Coming to Town, Feliz Navidad, Last Christmas, Deck the Halls. Labels are song titles (not recordings); all versions count. Computed order (average position over 10 people sources: YouGov 2020, YouGov 2019, Monmouth 2022, Saint Leo 2016, ASCAP 2023, Spotify streams, CardsChat Spotify playlists, Wildgoose search, Play USA search, P1 Media listener appeal; missing = list length + 5; AP-NORC 2018 and Statista 2025 report too few items to average and are used as corroboration): 1 All I Want for Christmas Is You 6.1, 2 Jingle Bells 9.9, 3 Rudolph 10.5, 4 Jingle Bell Rock 10.9, 5 White Christmas 11.0, 6 Feliz Navidad 13.7, 7 Santa Claus Is Coming to Town 14.1, 8 Let It Snow 14.6, 9 Carol of the Bells 15.1, 10 Last Christmas 15.8, 11 Rockin' Around 16.1, 12 Winter Wonderland 16.5, 13 Frosty 17.2, 14 We Wish You 17.9, 15 The Christmas Song 18.5, 16 Silent Night 19.2, 17 Most Wonderful Time 19.6, 18 It's Beginning 19.8, 19 Have Yourself 19.9, 20 Holly Jolly 21.2, 21 Santa Tell Me 23.3, 22 Sleigh Ride 24.2, 23 Deck the Halls 24.3, 24 This Christmas 25.2, 25 Joy to the World 25.5, 26 O Holy Night 25.7, 27 Here Comes Santa Claus 25.7, 30 Little Drummer Boy 29.1, 36 Silver Bells 30.1. Moves: (1) Silent Night 16 -> 3. It is #1 in every favorite poll (YouGov 2019 and 2020, Monmouth 2022, Saint Leo 2016, AP-NORC 2018) and #2 in Play USA search and #11 in Wildgoose search. Its low average comes only from sources that cannot contain it: ASCAP covers copyrighted songs only (Silent Night is public domain), P1 tests secular radio recordings only (105 penalty), and the streaming top-10/20 lists measure single recordings. Gut check #3. (2) Rudolph and Jingle Bell Rock swap with White Christmas: White Christmas 5 -> 4 because it is #2 in YouGov 2019 and Saint Leo, #5 in YouGov 2020 and Monmouth, ahead of Rudolph and Jingle Bell Rock in every favorite poll; Rudolph 3 -> 5 and Jingle Bell Rock 4 -> 6 lead it only on search, ASCAP and radio appeal. Small move inside the top 6. (3) Frosty 13 -> 8 (gut check): Wildgoose search #5 (1.18M), ASCAP #14, Saint Leo #21; no source puts it below Let It Snow, Carol of the Bells or Winter Wonderland on naming/search except P1 radio appeal (#27). (4) Rockin' Around 11 -> 9 (gut check): Spotify #3, CardsChat #2, P1 #4, Play USA #5, ASCAP #7. (5) Santa Claus Is Coming to Town 7 -> 10 and Last Christmas 10 -> 11, Let It Snow 8 -> 12, Carol of the Bells 9 -> 13: these shift down to make room for moves 1, 3, 4; relative order kept except Let It Snow/Carol, which follow the computed order after Santa Claus and Last Christmas (both in the gut check). (6) Deck the Halls 23 -> 20 only: it is in the gut check, but sources put it lower: Wildgoose search #18 (behind Carol of the Bells, Winter Wonderland, Let It Snow, O Holy Night), ASCAP #18, P1 #41 recording, and it is not named in any favorite poll (Monmouth, both YouGovs, Saint Leo top 38). So it is not lifted into the top 12. (7) O Holy Night 26 -> 22 and Joy to the World 25 -> 23, ahead of Santa Tell Me (21 -> 24): the two hymns rank high in the general-public favorite polls (O Holy Night #3 YouGov 2020, #3 YouGov 2019, #2 Monmouth; Joy to the World #5 Saint Leo, #7 Monmouth, #19 Wildgoose search) and are penalised by the same public-domain/secular-radio gaps as Silent Night; Santa Tell Me leads only on streaming and is unlikely to be a typical adult's spontaneous answer. Sleigh Ride (22) and This Christmas (24) drop out to make room; Sleigh Ride is #25 by the computed order once O Holy Night and Joy move up. Left out: The Twelve Days of Christmas (Wildgoose search #8, but in no other source read), Little Drummer Boy (favorite polls #6-9 but absent from streaming/search/ASCAP lists), Mary Did You Know, Silver Bells, Here Comes Santa Claus, Grandma Got Run Over by a Reindeer, Blue Christmas, Baby It's Cold Outside. No alias uses bare 'santa', 'christmas', 'jingle' or 'snow' to avoid collisions.
confidence: High for 1-5 (AIWFC, Jingle Bells, Silent Night, White Christmas, Rudolph all have 6+ people sources and top-5 placements in polls and search). Medium for 6-12: the order among Jingle Bell Rock, Feliz Navidad, Frosty, Rockin', Santa Claus, Last Christmas, Let It Snow depends on whether search/streaming or favorite polls weigh more; these are favorite polls, not free-naming polls, so recall of upbeat secular songs is under-measured there. Medium-low for 13-24: tail mixes radio/streaming staples with hymns, judged by source type. Caveats: Billboard's all-time Holiday 100 page was paywalled (402) and not used; Saint Leo is from 2016; the Wildgoose and Play USA search studies are marketing studies; P1 and ASCAP measure recordings and copyrighted songs only.
